title: Keepalive ping storm — playbook draft
summary: Between 2029-06-14T00:22 and 2029-06-14T01:05 UTC we experienced a significant degradation of hosted API streaming and short-generation latencies caused by an influx of client keepalive pings from a misbehaving SDK cohort. Symptoms included p95/p99 latency increases, a burst of 502/504s at the edge, and an elevated rate of streaming fragment reassembly failures. The burst affected ~18% of streaming sessions in US-west and produced service errors for several high-traffic customers.
impact: ~18% of active streaming sessions experienced mid-request disconnects or fragmented responses; non-streaming short generations saw p95 latency increase from 120ms to 550ms for ~10 minutes. No data loss was detected in user payloads. Several customers reported degraded UX; a small set triggered automated retries that amplified load on acceptor queues.
detection: Alert: ephemeral-acceptor-queue-depth > 80% for multiple edge pods (alert rule: sre.edge.acceptor.queue.depth.high). Additional signal from streaming-fragment-errors metric and a spike in edge TCP resets. Oncall page had an automated alert at 2029-06-14T00:24 UTC.
timeline:
2029-06-14T00:22 UTC - First acceptor-queue-depth alert triggered
2029-06-14T00:23 UTC - Streaming fragment error rate rises above baseline
2029-06-14T00:25 UTC - Pager notified SRE primary (Devon)
2029-06-14T00:28 UTC - Triage: surge of tiny keepalive frames observed from a small set of client IPs / SDK-version header 'ri-sdk/3.2.1'
2029-06-14T00:31 UTC - Mitigation: emergency ingress rate-limit rule deployed on edge ingress layer to aggregate/quotas small keepalive frames
2029-06-14T00:36 UTC - Immediate improvement in acceptor-queue depth, p95 latency begins returning toward normal
2029-06-14T00:45 UTC - Hotfix to streaming muxer deployed to coalesce adjacent keepalive frames (edge repo PR merged)
immediate_mitigation: 1) Deploy temporary ingress rate-limit that treats keepalive/keep-alive frame pattern as lower-priority and caps per-connection keepalive rate to 1/sec. 2) Hotpatch streaming muxer to coalesce contiguous keepalive frames and avoid scheduling a separate acceptor task per keepalive. 3) Throttle retries from downstream retry middleware via short-circuit on known SDK version header.
root_cause: A rolling client SDK release (ri-sdk/3.2.1) introduced a regression in its keepalive logic causing certain clients to emit keepalive PINGS at an aggressive cadence (10–20x intended). This interacted poorly with the edge acceptor design: each keepalive created a tiny work item that bypassed batching and caused acceptor-thread thrash and small-window TCP churn. Amplifying factors: automated client retries and a lack of aggregation for sub-10-byte frames at the ingress layer.
long_term_mitigations: Add server-side keepalive aggregation at the edge ingress so sub-64-byte keepalives are combined for a single acceptor enqueue operation
Introduce an SDK compatibility gate: detect ri-sdk/3.2.x and apply conservative per-connection heuristics until clients are upgraded
Update SLAs and telemetry: add dedicated metric for keepalive-influence on acceptor queue and on streaming reassembly errors
Customer communication play: automated warning to customers using ri-sdk/3.2.1 with recommended upgrade to 3.2.3
Improve retry middleware to be idempotent-aware and rate-limited to avoid amplifying short-duration spikes

runbook_steps: Step 0: Acknowledge pager and post short summary to #sre-incidents with incident id
Step 1: Check acceptor queue panels and streaming-fragment-errors; capture current node list and p95/p99 latencies
Step 2: Identify top source IPs/SDK headers causing spike (query edge logs: frames < 64B grouped by user-agent and ip)
Step 3: If spike source is small cohort with SDK header, deploy temporary ingress rate-limit rule targeting that header and IP CIDRs
Step 4: Deploy streaming muxer coalescing hotpatch if available; otherwise enable ingress aggregation and remove at steady state
Step 5: Monitor metrics for 15 minutes; if no improvement, escalate to platform infra and product for customer communications
Step 6: After stabilization, run a post-incident data pull for affected customers and estimate customer impact window
oncall_notes: When paging, prioritize connection-level signals over aggregate token metrics for this class of incidents. Keep an eye on tiny-frame histograms and the 'acceptor-enqueue-per-second' metric which climbs sharply during a ping storm. If you see large numbers of distinct ephemeral-stream-ids with near-zero payload, that indicates a keepalive amplification pattern. Use the 'ingress hotpatch' runbook entry to apply the temporary rule; it is designed to be safe for 1-hour windows and reversible.
postmortem_notes: Draft: this incident demonstrates a class of low-CPU but high-IO work items (tiny frames) that are inefficient for our current acceptor threading model. Prioritizing aggregation for tiny frames and adding heuristics for known-bad SDK versions will materially reduce surface area for similar future incidents. Final postmortem will include customer impact matrix and retrospective on SDK release processes.
notes: Observed correlation between customer's retry middleware and increased keepalive churn; recommended follow-up: contact three largest affected customers for root-cause info on their side. Consider adding a CI gate that runs a simulated keepalive storm against the edge canary during SDK releases.
